THE METHOD

A transparent path from peaks to candidates.

01 / NARROW THE SEARCH

Start with molecular mass.

Subtract the selected adduct from precursor m/z. Keep reference compounds within the chosen tolerance, with a 0.006 Da minimum window.

02 / COMPARE FRAGMENTS

Find a spectral resemblance.

Normalize intensities, keep up to 100 peaks above 1%, and bin at 0.1 Da. Compare vectors weighted by √intensity × √(m/z ÷ 100).

03 / INSPECT THE EVIDENCE

Make the result explainable.

Rank compounds by their best reference cosine score. Compare peaks, inspect candidate structures, and explore possible neutral losses.

PROJECT NOTES

Built to make the research tangible.

This interactive companion to the Enveda CASMI 2026 project adapts the team's mass-filtered spectral retrieval baseline for the browser.

My research contribution. I studied competition materials, investigated diagnostic fragment-ion and neutral-loss resources, and proposed exploring chemistry-informed approaches and domain-specific Transformer architectures in our team discussions.

This demonstration. A newly built browser interface for spectral search, candidate comparison, peak visualization, and source inspection.

Explore the project on GitHub ↗

What this demo shows

Real computation on a curated library of four compounds. Each example uses a different recorded spectrum from the eight reference spectra. They are not independent molecules or a validation benchmark.

It does not run the full CASMI pipeline, neural models, or de novo structure generation. A high match cannot establish a molecule's identity; compounds absent from this library cannot be identified.

Data: MassBank records by Tobias Schulze and Martin Krauss, Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ), under CC0. Peaks are normalized for this interface. Structures are drawn from the records' SMILES.
